subject: Responsibility split & transfer-addendum: Order Form + DPA coordination
body:
--- Message 1 (oldest) ---
From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@cardinalhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Gray <tom.gray@cardinalhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Jul 2028 09:15:22 -0400
Subject: Cardinal Health - redlines on DPA + order form (SCCs / role split questions)

Hi Ben & Karthik,

Thanks again for the call last week. We've attached our legal team's redlines to the DPA and a marked-up order form for the subscription pricing. A few things our counsel specifically asked us to confirm before we proceed to signature:

- SCCs: we saw the reference to SCCs in the DPA but the role allocation section is unclear about whether Cardinal is the data exporter for the telemetry logs and whether Redwood will be a processor or a controller for business reporting. Can you confirm the splitter language you're proposing?
- Processor/subprocessor list: we need a snapshot of the current subprocessors for hosted API and an indication of whether Redwood's Dedicated offering (VPC) changes any obligations.
- Transfer-impact addendum: counsel asked whether Redwood can provide a short transfer-impact addendum to accompany the DPA (one-page summary + hosting/region commitments).

We attached: Cardinal_DPA_Redline.docx and OrderForm_v2-redline.pdf. Can you review and let us know next steps and expected timing for an updated draft? We have internal approval cadence and would like to keep to the pricing window discussed.

Best,
Elena
General Counsel (Contracts)
Cardinal Health

[Attachment: Cardinal_DPA_Redline.docx (docx, 42 KB)]
[Attachment: OrderForm_v2-redline.pdf (pdf, 95 KB)]

--- Message 2 ---
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Jul 2028 11:03:10 -0400
Subject: Re: Cardinal Health - redlines on DPA + order form (SCCs / role split questions)

Elena — thanks for sending these over and for flagging the timing. I’ve looped in our legal lead, Laura, to review the redlines and respond on SCCs/roles and the transfer-addendum ask.

We’ll aim to get an initial legal response + a tracked draft back within 48 hours. If any points require escalation (e.g., carveouts for training data or KMS routing), Laura will flag and we can schedule a short call with Cardinal counsel.

Quick ask on our side: can you confirm the primary dataset streams Cardinal is most concerned about (telemetry vs PHI-enriched product logs)? That will help prioritise the evidence for processor responsibilities.

Best,
Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

--- Message 3 ---
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@cardinalhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 10:20:33 -04:00
Subject: Re: Cardinal Health - redlines on DPA + order form (SCCs / role split questions)

Hi Elena — appreciated, and thanks Ben for the intro. I reviewed the attached redlines and put together an internal-first pass. Summary below, then inline notes in the attached DPA_redline_lawyers.docx.

Summary of proposed positions:
- SCCs & role allocation: Redwood proposes the following pragmatic allocation: Cardinal = Exporter/Controller for customer-supplied PHI/enrichment; Redwood = Processor for model inference and telemetry while acting as Controller only for aggregated product analytics (non-identifiable). We have a short clause that captures this split and a fallback for emergent regulatory requests.
- Transfer-impact addendum: we can provide a one-page addendum summarising hosting regions, KMS options (customer-managed KMS supported in Dedicated/Private), and subprocessor snapshot. We'll include a narrow statement about retention and deletion windows.
- Subprocessors: we will supplement the DPA with a current subprocessor list and a commitment to 30 days' notice for new subprocessors. For Dedicated/VPC customers we can also include additional language limiting cross-region backups.
- Order form redlines: pricing redline comments look OK; however, the liability and warranty aggregation needs a short revision (see para 4 in our doc).

Attachments: DPA_redline_lawyers.docx (tracked) and internal note DPA_internal_note.txt.

Next steps we propose:
1) I’ll send a tracked DPA incorporating our SCCs language and a draft transfer-impact addendum by EOD tomorrow.
2) If Cardinal counsel has carveouts, we can do one negotiated pass; anything beyond that will need a quick escalation path (we’ll flag to Revenue Ops).
3) Ben / Karthik: please confirm the business dataset priority (Elena's earlier question) so we pick the right clause for telemetry vs PHI.

If you prefer a call, I’m available Wed 13:00–15:00 ET.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: DPA_redline_lawyers.docx (docx, 58 KB)]
[Attachment: DPA_internal_note.txt (txt, 4 KB)]

--- Message 4 ---
From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@cardinalhealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Gray <tom.gray@cardinalhealth.com>, Baker & Co. Counsel <bgclaw@bakerco.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jul 2028 08:42:07 -04:00
Subject: Re: Cardinal Health - redlines on DPA + order form (SCCs / role split questions)

Laura — thank you for the quick review and clear summary. A couple of follow-ups from our side after an internal huddle:

- Primary datasets: telemetry logs + product usage metrics. We do not plan to send PHI-enriched payloads to Redwood for the initial pilot. The split you suggested sounds workable for the pilot.
- Subprocessor snapshot: pls include both hosted and dedicated subprocessors and indicate which subprocessors can appear in backups or S3 replication (Tom is particularly concerned about cross-border replication).
- Transfer-impact addendum: a one-page summary is ideal. Also, is there a way to state in the addendum that Dedicated/VPC customers with customer-managed KMS will be treated as "onshore-equivalent" for transfer purposes? Our counsel would like that option made explicit if possible.

Baker & Co. (copied) will look through Laura's tracked doc and come back with any redline-specific asks. If it helps speed things up, we can do a 30-minute sync tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Elena

--- Message 5 (newest) ---
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@cardinalhealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Tom Gray <tom.gray@cardinalhealth.com>, Baker & Co. Counsel <bgclaw@bakerco.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jul 2028 16:22:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Cardinal Health - redlines on DPA + order form (SCCs / role split questions)

Thanks all — quick operational note and proposed path forward so we have clear owners and timeline:

1) Laura to deliver tracked DPA + one-page transfer-impact addendum (with optional sentence for Dedicated/VPC + customer-managed KMS) by EOD tomorrow (Thu 12 Jul).
2) Baker & Co. to provide any narrow redline requests within 48 hours of delivery.
3) Ben/Karthik to align order form pricing and sign-off window; if legal approves the DPA language we’ll pull the pricing hold and move to signature.
4) Tech ops (we will send subprocessor snapshot) — we’ll include flags for cross-border backups and replication.

I’ll set a 30-minute call Thurs 09:30 ET to walk the small set of open points — invite to follow. If there are any blocking redlines after Baker & Co’s pass, please escalate to Laura and me immediately so we can route to Revenue Ops.

Attachments in thread: Cardinal_DPA_Redline.docx, OrderForm_v2-redline.pdf, DPA_redline_lawyers.docx, DPA_internal_note.txt
Drive link for legal draft: https://drive.redwood.com/links/cardinal/dpa-redlines
DocuSign intent/placeholder: https://app.docusign.com/nebula/recipient/12345-Cardinal-DPA

Thanks,
Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
